elements.content: Communication Goal: I can talk about past places and feelings, tell a simple past story, and ask about past events.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0-A1 General English
- Unit: Inspired Module 7. Looking Back
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Looking Back
- Materials: Weekend cards, past verb cards, timeline, photo prompts.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use was/were for past states
• narrate with regular and irregular past verbs
• ask Did you...? and Wh- questions
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles present simple, routines, and free-time vocabulary.

Next lesson: Lesson 8 recycles past experiences in a now-then-next synthesis.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

tired — needing rest. Example: I was tired last night.
busy — having a lot to do. Example: She is busy today.
great — very good. Example: The trip was great.
terrible — very bad. Example: The weather was terrible.
cold — having a low temperature. Example: It is cold in winter.
sunny — with a lot of sun. Example: Last Saturday was sunny.
home — the place where you live. Example: I was at home.
work — a job or activity you do. Example: I work in an office.
holiday — a time when you do not work. Example: We go on holiday in July.
trip — a journey to a place. Example: I took a trip to the coast.
market — a place where people buy and sell food. Example: I went to the market.
friend — a person you like and know well. Example: Tom is my best friend.
train — a vehicle that runs on rails. Example: We take the train at eight.
photos — pictures taken with a camera. Example: I took photos at the market.
gift — a present for someone. Example: I bought a gift for my friend.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Where were you last night? — I was at a concert. (asking about a past place)
• It was amazing. (describing a past feeling)
• I worked from home yesterday. (past regular verb)
• We didn't cook. We ordered pizza. (past negative)
• I went to the market and bought fruit. (past irregular verbs)
• Did you have a good weekend? — Yes, I did. (past yes/no question)
• What did you do? (past wh- question)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'needing rest'?
Which word means 'having a lot to do'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Past -ed endings and past question intonation

worked /wɜːkt/ — voiceless /t/ ending
called /kɔːld/ — voiced /d/ ending
visited /ˈvɪzɪtɪd/ — extra /ɪd/ syllable
went /went/ — irregular past
Listen and repeat:
I worked from home. I called my sister. I visited a museum. Did you have a good weekend?
Mark the stressed syllable in these words:

elements.placeholder: Mark the stress: worked, called, visited

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use the past simple to talk about finished actions in the past.

Form:
Past simple: regular verbs: Regular verbs add -ed: work → worked. Negative: didn't + base verb. Question: Did + subject + base verb?

Examples:
• I worked yesterday.
• She visited her friend.
• We didn't watch TV.
• Did you call him?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I ___ my friend yesterday.
She ___ TV last night.
We ___ work on Sunday.
___ you call him?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• Yesterday, I ... (work / visit / play) ...
• Last weekend, she ...
• I didn't ... yesterday.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What did you do yesterday?
• Where did you go last weekend?
• Did you study English last week?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about yesterday with regular past verbs.
• Write three sentences about last weekend.
Reading: Looking Back

Last weekend, Marta went to Porto with her sister. They took an early flight on Saturday morning. The weather was sunny and warm. They walked along the river, ate fresh fish, and visited a famous bookshop. They didn't rent a car because the metro was easy. Ben didn't travel. He stayed in the city. On Saturday night, he met two old friends and saw a live jazz band. On Sunday, he cleaned his apartment and cooked a big curry.
Where did Marta go?
Did Ben travel last weekend?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How was your weekend?
B: It was really good. On Saturday I went to the farmers' market and bought fresh vegetables. Then I visited my brother.
A: Did you go out on Saturday night?
B: No, I didn't. I was tired, so I stayed home and watched a documentary.
A: I took the train to the coast on Sunday. The beach was quiet, and I had lunch at a seafood cafe.
What did the first speaker buy?
Did the first speaker go out on Saturday night?
Speaking task: Tell your partner about last weekend. Ask four follow-up questions with Did you...? and What/Where/Who.

• Where were you last weekend?
• How was it?
• What did you do?
• Did you meet anyone?
• What was the best part?
Role-play: You are at a Monday coffee chat. Swap one recent experience and ask at least four past questions.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write six sentences about a recent day or weekend. Use was/were, one negative, and three past verbs.
Model: Last weekend, I was ... I went ... I didn't ... It was ...
